blocks.text: For decades, the place to see all of Turkmenistan in one morning was a market on the northern edge of Ashgabat, where the city meets the Karakum desert. Its everyday name, Tolkuçka (in English often Tolkuchka), is a Russian word for a crowded flea market where you push your way through; in Turkmen it is the *jygyldyk*.

**History.** The flea market began after the Second World War in the south of the city and moved several times. By 1972 it had settled at Choganly, near the airport, on the far side of the Karakum Canal at the edge of the desert, and its grounds were paved. In the 1990s it became famous as a classic Central Asian bazaar: hundreds of small traders selling carpets and all kinds of small goods, and camels wandering between the stalls.

**The new bazaar.** In February 2011 the old market closed, and a new one, officially *Altyn Asyr*, opened further north. It covers 154 hectares, with more than two thousand shops, a hotel and cafés; seen from above, its plan copies a carpet ornament of Ahal province, and a tall clock tower stands at its centre. People still call it Tolkuçka, or *Täze jygyldyk*, the new jygyldyk. Travel writers who knew the old site miss its atmosphere, while granting that the new one is cleaner and gives more shade from the desert sun.

**What you find.** Almost everything: carpets new and old, telpeks, embroidered dresses and skullcaps, silver jewellery, silk, spices, household goods and clothes. In the livestock section people trade sheep, goats and camels; a new camel goes home in a truck, or walks. The market is busiest at the weekend, from early morning to early afternoon; Lonely Planet's guide names Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.

blocks.title: This unit's words at the bazaar
blocks.text: *halyçy*, carpet weaver; *telpekçi*, telpek maker; *satyjy* and *alyjy*, seller and buyer; *maryly* or *aşgabatly*, from Mary or Ashgabat; and for a small purchase, *kiçijik*.
With this unit's grammar, you can read this:

blocks.tk: Tolkuçka Aşgabadyň iň uly bazary. Bu ýerde halyçylar, telpekçiler we zergärler bar. Satyjylar dürli welaýatlardan gelýärler. Bazaryň bir böleginde düýe we goýun satýarlar. Bir oglanjyk kiçijik düýä seredip, gülüp dur.
blocks.en: Tolkuçka is the biggest market in Ashgabat. Here there are carpet weavers, telpek makers and jewellers. The sellers come from different provinces. In one part of the bazaar they sell camels and sheep. A little boy is looking at a tiny camel and laughing.

options: on the northern edge of Ashgabat, by the desert

questions.q: When did the new Altyn Asyr bazaar open?
questions.explain: In February 2011; 1972 is when the old market was already at Choganly.

questions.q: In the reading, what is the little boy doing?
options: looking at a tiny camel and laughing
questions.explain: *kiçijik düýä seredip, gülüp dur*: looking at the tiny camel, he is laughing.
